description: Ceiling classification of Σ(2,3,5) S-matrix objects vs the b₄ physicality bound m<1/√5. Primary entries (S_00,S_01,φ⁻¹) overshoot; only secondary powers fall below and none is forced — the icosahedral-m lead does not yet supply a forward parameter-free m. scope-(a); no AME fit.

assertions.name: primary_icosahedral_objects_overshoot_ceiling
assertions.source: S_00=1/D=0.5257, S_01=φ/D=0.8507, φ⁻¹=0.6180 all EXCEED 1/√5=0.4472 — the naive Σ(2,3,5) vacuum-row entries and the golden ratio itself are NOT admissible as m (det(I+mS)<0, unphysical). So the forward m is NOT the primary S-matrix entry.

assertions.name: forward_m_not_uniquely_singled_out
assertions.source: 3 distinct icosahedral objects fall BELOW the ceiling (φ⁻²=0.382, 1/D²=0.276, sin²(π/5)=0.345, …) — no single one is structurally forced as m. Selecting the one that matches AME would be the forbidden back-solve (the 'seventh ansatz'); a forward derivation needs extra structure not yet present.

result.verdict: SCOPE-(a) NARROWING of the icosahedral-m lead (NOT a closure, NOT a refutation). The 1/√5 ceiling is genuinely √5/binary-icosahedral, but the PRIMARY Σ(2,3,5) objects — S_00=0.526, S_01=0.851, φ⁻¹=0.618 — all OVERSHOOT the ceiling (unphysical as m), as does the corpus z_naive=0.499. Only SECONDARY powers/combinations fall below (φ⁻²=0.382, 1/D²=0.276, sin²(π/5)=0.345), and no single one is structurally forced. CONSEQUENCE: the 'pin m to the icosahedral S-matrix' lead does NOT yet supply a parameter-free m — the forward selection among sub-ceiling candidates is unresolved, and choosing by AME match is the forbidden fit. The lead is SUGGESTIVE (√5 ceiling = icosahedral, and Σ(2,3,5) is the keystone object) but needs additional structure — most naturally the SAME archimedean continuation the keystone τ derivation needs (Frontier B): the S-matrix lives at the root-of-unity fibre, the physical m at real q₀. The two frontiers share the fibre→observable wall. No fit; no c_k wired.
